ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1 Zero-price bypass: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, validateHandlerOrder does not check for sqrtPriceX96==0 while _validatePricingBounds does
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: validateHandlerOrder is view-only (no state changes). CLOB fills use stored currentPrice, not computed price. The zero bypass only affects the advisory pricing bounds check during order placement, not the actual fill math. No extraction path exists.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2 Direct handler call: calling CLOBTransferHandler.executeSwap() directly bypasses pricing enforcement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler has no executeSwap function. ammHandleTransfer requires msg.sender == AMM (line 230). All CLOB entry points (deposit, withdraw, openOrder, closeOrder) are user-facing and don't bypass hooks. ammHandleTransfer is only callable by the AMM during swap settlement.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3 Settings sync gap: setTokenSettings may leave stale memSettings in CreatorHookSettingsRegistry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: This is confirmed pattern CP-005 (v1-L03). It causes redundant storage writes (gas waste) but no value extraction. The initialized field cannot desync in a way that bypasses security checks because both paths write to the same storage slot.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4 Transient storage leak: DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT not cleared on all paths
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: This is confirmed pattern CP-001 (HOOK-001). The slot is written in beforeSwap (line 839) for direct swaps and read in afterSwap (lines 843-844). When afterSwap flag is disabled but beforeSwap is enabled for a second swap in the same tx, afterSwap reads stale data. However, this requires specific flag configuration (beforeSwap enabled + afterSwap disabled) which is creator-controlled. Impact is limited to incorrect pricing bounds validation for the second swap's afterSwap, which is a Low severity issue already known.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Flash loan + CLOB price distortion: use one venue to move price, extract on another
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB orders are placed at maker-specified prices and filled at those prices. There is no shared oracle between AMM pools and CLOB. Flash loan cannot move CLOB prices because CLOB prices are set by individual maker orders, not by an AMM curve.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: SingleProviderPoolType oracle spoof via controlled hook: malicious hook returns extreme price
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool hook is set at pool creation by the LP and cannot be changed. The price is bounded by MIN_SQRT_RATIO/MAX_SQRT_RATIO check (SingleProviderPoolType.sol:328-330). A malicious LP creating a pool with a manipulated hook can only harm users who voluntarily swap through that pool — this is Tier B exploitability (requires custom handler). The LP is the victim if they set bad prices (self-inflicted).
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: SingleProviderPoolType.sol:323-330 (price bounds check + onlyAMM modifier)

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Direct swap bypasses pricing bounds checked by hooks
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Direct swaps DO execute beforeSwap and afterSwap hooks (AMMModule.sol:1836-1838). In _validatePricingBounds, when poolType is address(0) (direct swap), beforeSwap stores the amount in transient storage and afterSwap computes the price from both amounts. Pricing bounds ARE enforced for direct swaps, just via a different mechanism (transient storage + computeRatioX96 instead of pool's getCurrentPriceX96).
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: AMMModule.sol:1836-1847 (hooks called) + AMMStandardHook.sol:838-851 (direct swap pricing)

ruled_out_vectors.vector: snapPrice in addLiquidity allows arbitrary price movement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: addLiquidity in DynamicPoolType does NOT change the pool price (sqrtPriceX96). It adds liquidity at the current price range. The pool price only moves during swaps (computeSwap). Sandwich around addLiquidity is not possible because adding liquidity doesn't move price.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: DynamicHelper.sol:55-100 (modifyPosition does not change pool.sqrtPriceX96)

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Dust-loop extraction: 100+ tiny swaps leak value to attacker each iteration
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Rounding in SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, and all pool types favors the protocol (uses mulDivRoundingUp for amounts charged TO user, mulDiv for amounts paid TO user). Fuzz testing 27 tests x 25+ runs confirms no round-trip profit at realistic amounts. At extreme amounts near price bounds, rounding can compound to 1 wei per operation which is not economically viable after gas costs.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Bypass slippage/deadline params to extract value
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Slippage is enforced at the AMM level: singleSwap checks amountSpecified against limitAmount, directSwap checks maxAmountOut/minAmountIn. These are user-specified parameters that cannot be manipulated by an attacker. Deadline is checked in the entry point before any swap logic runs.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: AMMModule.sol:1852-1854 (limitAmount check) + LimitBreakAMM.sol:189-200 (entry point checks)

theft_theses.thesis: Flash loan + CLOB price manipulation: borrow large, move AMM price, exploit CLOB orders at stale prices
theft_theses.victim: CLOB makers with orders at pre-manipulation prices
theft_theses.asset: Token difference between AMM-distorted and CLOB-stated prices

theft_theses.thesis: Controlled hook returns fake sqrtPriceX96 in SingleProviderPool, attacker swaps at rigged price
theft_theses.asset: Token output difference at manipulated vs fair price

theft_theses.thesis: Dust-loop rounding extraction: iterated 1-wei swaps compound rounding errors
theft_theses.victim: LP reserves in any pool type
theft_theses.asset: Accumulated rounding dust over thousands of swaps
